subject: Clarify: SOC 2 Type II docs, SIG/CAIQ and hosting/control-plane boundaries
messages:
From: Claire Mendoza <claire.mendoza@eurobank.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: audits@eurobank.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 14:18:02 +0000
Subject: SOC 2 Type II + SIG/CAIQ — hosting boundary and KMS questions

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. Our security team ran a quick pass on Redwood's materials and asked for a few clarifications before we move to the formal risk sign-off:

- We need the SOC 2 Type II report covering at least the last 12 months and the audit window dates. Can you confirm the audited period you have available and whether a bridge letter will be provided when the report ends outside our procurement window?
- In the SIG/CAIQ response we saw a note that the inference control plane is hosted out of the US but customer data and inference workloads can be pinned to EU regions. Can you confirm: does any customer plaintext data (or unencrypted KV cache) transit or persist in the US for EU-hosted workloads?
- Key management: do you offer a customer-managed key (KMS) flow / HSM integration for dedicated or private deployments? If so, which cloud KMS providers are supported and where are the keys physically stored?

If you can attach the SOC 2 PDF (or redacted excerpt), a short control-plane diagram, and a SIG excerpt, that would help our auditors. We're targeting an internal go/no-go on Monday.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Mendoza
Senior Security PM — Third-Party Risk
EuroBank Group

P.S. We may follow up with a narrow CAIQ ask but wanted to get these high-level points resolved first.

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Mendoza <claire.mendoza@eurobank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 16:02:10 +0000
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II + SIG/CAIQ — hosting boundary and KMS questions

Claire — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses below and I attached the requested artifacts to this thread (SOC 2 PDF + SIG excerpt + a one-page control-plane diagram).

- SOC 2 Type II: attached is our most recent Type II report (audit period 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30). We can provide a signed bridge letter if your procurement window requires coverage past 2026-06-30 — standard wording confirms continuity of controls and the next audit timeline. If you prefer we can tailor the bridge wording to explicitly reference data residency and routing guarantees.

- Hosting vs control plane: For hosted / shared customers (Redwood API), the inference data plane (model execution, KV/prefix caching, and any persisted inference artifacts) can be pinned to an EU region (we currently support eu-west-1 and eu-central-1). The control plane (orchestration, telemetry, routing policy decisions) is in a separate management region that is US-based by default for hosted customers. Critically: plaintext customer request/response pairs are NOT persisted in the US when you select EU-hosted data plane; the only metadata sent to the control plane for routing is non-sensitive (request size, region affinity, model version) and we can provide a minimized telemetry profile for your auditors.

- Cross-border cache replication: we do not replicate KV caches cross-region by default for pinned EU data planes. Caches are region-scoped unless you opt into multi-region replication for performance reasons.

- KMS/HSM: Yes — for Redwood Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys via Cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault). Keys can be provisioned in the customer-selected region; in Private deployments you retain full control (HSM/KMS in your VPC). For hosted customers we offer a Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) flow for tenant-level encryption keys; the key wrapping occurs in the region you select.

Attachments included: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025-07-01_to_2026-06-30.pdf, Redwood_SIG_Questionnaire_answers_excerpt.xlsx, control_plane_arch_diagram_v2.png

If useful I can loop in Marissa (Compliance) or Laura (Solutions for dedicated deployments) to provide the bridge-letter template and a sample DPA clause referencing cross-border processing. What timeline works for you on the bridge wording?

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Mendoza <claire.mendoza@eurobank.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: audits@eurobank.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:23:54 +0000
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II + SIG/CAIQ — hosting boundary and KMS questions

Thanks Ben — quick follow-ups from our audit team:

1) The auditors want explicit confirmation that the control-plane metadata sent to the US does not contain customer identifiers beyond a tenant ID hash (they asked for a short statement we can attach).

2) For BYOK: can you confirm whether key usage logs / key access audit events remain routable to the region where the KMS is hosted, or if any key usage telemetry is aggregated in the US control plane? Auditors often want proofs that key material and key-usage PII are never sent outside EU jurisdiction.

3) Lastly, do you have a short example bridge letter that names Redwood's next scheduled audit window / expected Type II report issuance date? Our procurement needs a dated commitment.

If you can get the three short confirmations (1–2 lines each) and the draft bridge letter by EOD today that would keep us on schedule.

Claire

[audits@eurobank.com]

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Mendoza <claire.mendoza@eurobank.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 14:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II + SIG/CAIQ — hosting boundary and KMS questions

Hi Claire — looping in a few short, auditor-friendly confirmations below and attaching our bridge-letter template in the portal link.

1) Control-plane metadata: Redwood confirms that metadata sent from EU-hosted data planes to our US control plane consists of non-identifying telemetry (tenant hash, model id, sequence length, request latency bucket) and does not include customer PII or raw request/response text. We will provide a signed statement on company letterhead for your file.

2) BYOK / key usage telemetry: For BYOK keys provisioned in an EU KMS, key-usage audit events (e.g., Encrypt/Decrypt call logs) are retained in the same region and are accessible to the tenant's KMS audit logs. Redwood does not persist key material. Any aggregated usage metrics sent to the control plane are non-identifiable and can be disabled upon request. For Private deployments, no key usage telemetry leaves the customer's network unless explicitly configured.

3) Bridge letter / audit timing: Our next audit is scheduled to cover 2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30 with the Type II report expected Q3 2027. We attached a standard bridge-letter template in the shared portal link; happy to add explicit wording about data residency upon request.

Please confirm if you want the signed letters (control-plane statement + bridge letter) sent as PDF attachments or uploaded to the portal link we shared.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance
Redwood Inference
